correctness.rationale: Translation of {0,d} has orbit size n except at even antipodal d=n/2, when it has size n/2; the gap classes exhaust distinct pairs. With R=n(d−1)+j+1, rotation reduces R by one for j>0 and increases it at wraparound. A b-move fixing the pair leaves R unchanged; b at {0,d} merges for d=1 and otherwise goes to {1,d} on the previous gap layer at index n−1, reducing R by one. The remaining zero-containing pair {n−d,0}, present only for 2d<n, moves to a larger gap layer, except at the top odd gap where its index instead increases to n−1. Thus exactly one letter drops R by one and no letter drops more; iterating the descending moves gives exactly the displayed word, and every geodesic must make those moves. The ranks fill contiguous disjoint layers, hence the spectrum, maximum, mean and composition follow. An independent reverse BFS enumerating inverse-letter images directly (including the single edge into the merged sink) checked ranks, unique optimal successors, and the resulting word for all 85,319 pairs with 3≤n≤80.
residual_risks: BFS is finite corroboration. The transition analysis proves the all-n claim only for the specified automaton and unit cost.

evidence: Record 261334d3d0c0 proves unique pair words cost-optimal for every positive choice of letter costs and explicitly states the unit-cost spectrum and nested paths. Gusev identifies the odd-order pair automaton but computes random-input expectations. The survey records the tight pair bound and generic backward trees. Gonze et al. treat distances in pair digraphs of permutations.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Taking both letter costs to be one covers the frozen problem exactly. Random input and pair distances under permutations are not the same optimization. The tight bound itself is established background.

evidence: The catalogue results include distinct pointwise distances, unique optima, and either the master word or explicitly optimal component counts. The known tight bound also forces at least one geodesic to visit every state of the pair digraph before the sink.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The unique maximal pair and the uniform mean follow by taking the maximum and arithmetic mean of the already given spectrum. The bivariate composition enumerator follows by summing over the covered words, so it does not furnish a separately distinct surviving claim.

evidence: The map x↦x−1 mod n sends b(0)=1 to b(n−1)=0 and preserves the rotation and letter names. Record fe81919abba1 gives a unique word of each distance as a suffix of W_n, with W_n=(a^(n−1)b)^((n−1)/2) for odd n and W_n=a^(n/2−1)b(a^(n−1)b)^(n/2−1) for even n.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The suffix of length n(d−1)+j+1 in that word is precisely a^j b(a^(n−1)b)^(d−1), including the truncated even antipodal layer. Thus master-word notation and separate geodesic formulas describe the same words for the same pairs.

evidence: Both catalogue records explicitly give the unit-multiplicity spectrum 1 through binom(n,2). The geodesic record gives the pointwise piecewise formula for sorted state pair {i,k}; the weighted record gives the componentwise minimal letter counts.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: For frozen gap d and index j, after shifting states, when j≥d the sorted lower state is i=n−j−1 and the ordered gap d; its formula nd−i gives the frozen length. When j<d, i=d−j−1 and the ordered gap is n−d; its formula (n+1)d−n−i gives the same length, including antipodal pairs. These formulas cover every entry of the frozen census, not just its maximum.

originality.rationale: Two distinct indexed records cover the frozen result under the state shift x↦x−1 mod n: one treats all positive letter costs, including unit costs; the other gives the same distances and unique geodesics as suffixes of its master word. This is demonstrable statement-level coverage, not a claim of priority between records.
residual_risks: The exact corpus overlap is established independently of publication ordering, including for the same-day match; primary historical priority is unresolved. No whole-paper exclusion is inferred for the inaccessible heuristics article.

value.rationale: Pointwise geometry of the natural extremal automaton would be useful beyond a bound, but the exact pointwise geometry, the spectrum and unique words are already covered, even under a stronger cost model. The mean, counts and enumerator are direct arithmetic summaries of those results, not a separate valuable remainder.
residual_risks: Does not discount the mathematical utility of the pair-geometry theorem itself or decide which record derived it first.
